newsitem.title: NORWAY: Justice minister quits in blow to Norway cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Justice minister quits in blow to Norway cabinet.

text.p: Anne Holt resigned on Tuesday as Norway's justice minister because of ill health, becoming the third cabinet member to quit the minority Labour government since it was formed just over three months ago.
Holt, 37, who has been on sick leave for several weeks suffering from anaemia, was a fresh face in the government put together last October 25 by Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland.

Holt's sudden resignation was a blow to Jagland, who has encountered major difficulties since succeeding veteran Gro Harlem Brundtland as head of government. Jagland faces a general election in September.

"Honestly, I cannot express my feelings," Jagland said in an emotional announcement of Holt's resignation. "I had looked forward to using the competence of this magnificent person in the government...But a human being's health comes first."
Gerd-Liv Valla, 48, deputy chairwoman of the Civil Servants Union, succeeded Holt, a lawyer and a best-seller writer of crime novels.
Two other key members of the original cabinet -- Terje Roed-Larsen at the national planning minister and Grete Faremo at energy -- have resigned in separate scandals in the past two months.

Jagland, seeking to avoid speculation Holt's resignation was dictated by political reasons, had the doctors' diagnosis with details of Holt's gynaecological examination and shortage of red blood corpuscles released to reporters.
"We are talking about the health of a human being, the health of a woman as you can see from the doctor's diagnosis," he said. "She needs complete rest to get well."

Holt and Roed-Larsen, both of whom are personal friends of Jagland, were touted at the time as dynamic personalities who would rejuvenate the 18-member government. It contained seven new names and four of the members retained from Brundtland's government shifted portfolios.
"I still think we have (new thinking), but you cannot find the same persons again when someone leaves," said Jagland, who is also Labour Party chairman.

Roed-Larsen, who quit as a U.N.-appointed Middle East mediator to join Jagland's government, resigned on November 27 amid a storm of media criticism over alleged irregularities in a share option deal he profited from in the mid-1980s.
On December 16, Oil and Energy Minister Grete Faremo was forced by Jagland to step down in a scandal over the national intelligence service's surveillance of a prominent left-wing politician.

Faremo was justice minister when the intelligence service in June last year started looking for dirt in the background of Berge Furre, a member of a parliamentary committee assigned to examine the work of the intelligence service itself.
